 Rigaku ZSX Primus XRF Standard Operating Procedure
1 Introduction
 1) Instrument features:
 > Wavelength Dispersive X-ray Fluorescence (WDXRF) systems with high
 resolution (typically 5 20 eV) and minimal spectral overlaps
 > Analysis of elements from Be to U
 > Tube above optics minimizes contamination issues
 > Micro analysis to analyze samples as small as 500 m
 > Mapping feature for elemental topography/distribution
 > Helium seal means the optics are always under vacuum
 2) Location
 Materials Characterization Core
 Room A119
 810 West Campus Drive
 West Haven, CT 06516
 3) Primary Staff Contact
 Dr. Min Li
 Tel: 203-737-8270
 Email: min.li@yale.edu
 Office: ESC II, Room E119D
The Yale West Campus MCC Facilities are operated for the benefit of all researchers. If you
encounter any problems with this facility, please contact the staff member listed above
immediately. There is never a penalty for asking questions. If the equipment is not behaving
exactly the way it should, contact a staff member.
Notice: Please follow strictly the SOP to keep the facility under good condition. Please DO NOT
explore the operation program unless approved by core manager.

2 PHA Analysis
 1) Using the green sample, in the sample ID setting window, click analysis Table (F7)
 a) Choose 1-Daily PHA and click OK
 b) Hit Analyze
 2) Click the tile windows in the upper right to see spectrometer status
 3) Once the measurement finishes, click the maintenance tab on the top, then select
 maintenance record, and the PHA adjustment
 a) Right click near the end of the curve (i.e. the current date) and select the PHA
 curve
 b) The PC curve should have a peak at a height of 200 and 6 kcps and the SC curve
 should have a peak at a height of 200 and 8 kcps
3 Setting up Application File
 1) Click Qual Application on the top of the program
 2) Select create new application
 a) Select Metal & Alloy
 b) Create an application name and choose a folder to save it in
 3) Move to element range
 a) Delete all elements already in the queue
 b) Select all the elements you want and they will appear yellow
 c) The elements must also be placed into fix angle column and to do this click Fix
 Angle Elem. and select each element again (they should appear blue)
 d) Click next
 4) The tab on the left will move to sample preparation
 a) If you have a powder sample in a prolene film you need to select prolene film
 after checking sample film otherwise (i.e. solid and trapped powders) leave this
 tab alone
 b) Click next
 5) The tab on the left will move to parameters
 a) Leave memo blank
 b) Select measuring diameter
 c) Leave vacuum on unless using liquid samples
 d) If using liquid samples, change sealing to In
 e) For component type select metal
 f) Leave balance alone unless you think there are possible impurities
 g) Do not use machine library
 h) Click next
 6) The tab on the left will move to check measuring parameters
 a) Double click on the elements that are in small percent
 b) If an element has a small concentration, change the step to 0.010 degrees and
 change the speed to 1-8 degrees/minute
 c) Under the FA elements you can adjust the peak location and allow the
 background and peak scans to go longer

Rigaku Primus II XRF
 d) Click next
 7) The tab on the left will move to Output Information
 a) Leave everything at the top clicked yes
 b) Can adjust the smoothing as desired
 c) Check "Output detection limit for undetected element"
 d) Click exit and the window should close
4 Start Scan
 1) To do a survey scan of all elements click EZ-scan
 2) For elemental scan, click sample ID
 a) Select Qual.
 b) Select position where sample is and change sample name
 c) Go to folder and find your application
 d) Do not select mapping
 e) Give file name and select folder in qldata (this folder is different than the
 application folder so you need to create a new folder)
 f) Click OK
 g) For addition sample, repeat for each spot
 h) For any unwanted created samples, right click on it and select cut
 i) Click analysis
5 Check Results
 1) Click Data Processing
 a) Select Qual Results
 1) Select SQX Calculation to determine mass percent of each element
 2) Select Qual Data Handling to see outputted spectra
